<header>IGNATIUS’S EPISTLE TO THE TRALLIANS, IX. X.</header>

...He destroyed the barrier <note>original: "phragmon"; a fence or hedge.</note> that had existed from the beginning, and the "middle wall of partition" <note>A reference to Ephesians 2:14, describing Christ reconciling Jews and Gentiles.</note> between us. He rose again after three days, His Father having raised Him; and after spending forty days with the Apostles, He was taken up to the Father. He sat down at His right hand, waiting until His enemies should be placed under His feet. Therefore, on the Preparation Day <note>Friday.</note>, at the third hour, He received the sentence from Pilate, the Father having permitted it. At the sixth hour He was crucified; at the ninth hour He gave up the spirit; and before the sun set, He was buried. Through the Sabbath He remained under the earth in the tomb where Joseph of Arimathea had laid Him. At the dawning of the Lord’s Day <note>Sunday.</note>, He rose from the dead, just as He Himself had said:
> Just as Jonah was in the belly of the whale for three days and three nights, so shall the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.

Therefore, the Preparation Day contains the Passion; the Sabbath contains the Burial; and the Lord’s Day contains the Resurrection.

## X.
But if, as some who are atheists—that is, unbelievers—say, He only became a man in appearance <term>Docetism<note>From the Greek word "dokein," meaning "to seem." These early heretics believed Christ’s physical body and suffering were mere illusions, as they felt matter was too corrupt for a divine being to inhabit.</note></term>, and did not truly take on a body; and that He only seemed to die and suffer, but did not truly do so: then for what reason am I in chains? And why do I pray to fight with wild beasts? If this is the case, I die for nothing. Furthermore, I would be speaking falsely about the cross of the Lord. And the prophet would also be proven wrong, saying:
> They shall look upon Him whom they pierced, and they shall mourn for themselves as for a beloved one.

Therefore, these people are unbelievers, no less so than those who actually crucified Him. But I do not place my hopes in one who died for me only in appearance, but in One who did so in reality; for a lie is foreign to the truth. Truly, then, Mary gave birth to a body that had God dwelling within it. And truly God the Word was born of the Virgin, clothed in a body of like passions to our own. He who forms all people in the womb was truly in the womb Himself, and fashioned a body for Himself from the seed of the Virgin, though without the intercourse of a man. He was carried in the womb, just as we are, for the required periods of time. And He was truly born, just as we are. He was truly nourished by milk, and shared in common food and drink, just as we are. Having lived among men for thirty years, He was truly baptized by John, and not merely in appearance. And having preached the Gospel for three years and performed signs and wonders, He was, by the false-Jews...

He broke down the fence <note>original Latin: "maceriam"; a stone wall or hedge.</note> which had existed from the beginning of the world, and dissolved its middle wall; and He rose again on the third day, the Father having raised Him up. After He had conversed with the Apostles for many days, He was taken up to the Father, and sat down at His right hand, waiting until all His enemies should be placed under His feet. Therefore, on the Preparation Day <note>Friday.</note>, at the third hour, He received the sentence from Pilate, with the Father’s permission. On the Lord’s Day <note>Sunday.</note> He rose from the dead, according to what He Himself had said:

Thus, the Preparation Day contains His passion, the Sabbath contains His burial and rest, and the Lord’s Day contains His resurrection.

## X.
But if, as some who are without God—that is, unbelievers and faithless—say, He was a man only in appearance <term>Docetism<note>An early Christian heresy (from the Greek "dokein," meaning "to seem") which taught that Christ's body was not human but phantasmal, and thus his suffering was not real.</note>, and did not take on a true body, and only seemingly suffered and died, then I am bound in chains for the sake of the Lord’s passion and death in vain, and I desire to fight with wild beasts to no purpose. If He suffered and died only in appearance and not in truth, then I am dying for nothing, having fashioned lies about the cross of the Lord. Moreover, the Prophet said in vain: 
> "They shall look upon Him whom they pierced, and they shall mourn over themselves as over a beloved one, and they shall grieve with a sorrow as if for a firstborn son." 

Therefore, those faithless and unbelieving people are no less guilty than those who crucified Him. But I have devoted myself to having hope in Him who truly died for me, because falsehood is foreign to Him. For Mary truly gave birth to a body, with God dwelling in it; and God the Word was truly born of the Virgin, putting on a body of like passions to ours, yet without sin. He was truly conceived in the womb and formed in the mother's body, fashioning and making for Himself a body from the Virgin—without the seed of a man, of course, or human intercourse. He was carried in the womb, just as we are carried for a time, and was truly nursed at the breast and nourished, just as we are. He partook of food and drink, just as we do, and when He was thirty years old, He was baptized by John in truth and not in a phantom <note>original: "phantasmate."</note>. and by Pilate the governor, the Judge was judged, was scourged, was slapped on the cheek, was spat upon; He wore a crown of thorns and a purple robe; He was condemned and truly crucified—not in appearance <note>Greek: "dokēsei"; the root of the word Docetism, a belief that Christ's body was an illusion.</note>, not in imagination, and not by deceit. Flee, then, from these atheistic heresies; for they are the inventions of the devil—that serpent, the author of evil, who through the woman deceived Adam, the father of our race.

### XI.
Flee also from his evil offshoots: Simon <note>Simon Magus, often cited by early Church fathers as the "father of all heresies."</note>, his firstborn son, and Menander, and Basilides, and all his roaring mass of wickedness—those man-worshippers, whom the prophet Jeremiah calls accursed. Flee also the unclean Nicolaitans <note>A group mentioned in the Book of Revelation, often associated with moral laxity.</note>, those who are falsely so-named, the lovers of pleasure, and the slanderers. For Nicholas, one of the apostles, was not such a man. Flee also the offspring of the wicked one, Theodotus and Cleobulus, who produce deadly fruit; if anyone tastes of it, they die immediately—not a temporary death, but the eternal one. These are not a planting of the Father, but cursed offspring. For "Every plant," says the Lord, "which my heavenly Father has not planted, shall be rooted up." For if they were branches of the Father, they would not be enemies of the cross of Christ, but rather of those who killed the Lord of glory. But now, by denying the cross and being ashamed of the passion, they cover up the lawlessness of the Jews—those who fight against God and are the killers of the Lord; for it is a small thing to call them killers of the prophets. But Christ invites you to His incorruptibility through His passion and resurrection, as you are His members.

wonders before the false Jews: and by Pilate the governor, the Judge was judged; He was scourged, He was struck with blows, He was spat upon; He wore a crown of thorns and a purple robe; He was condemned; He was truly crucified, willingly and well-pleasingly [to the Father], and not in appearance <note>Original: *phantastice*; a reference to Docetism, the belief that Jesus only "seemed" to have a physical body.</note>; nor did He die deceitfully, but truly; and He was buried, and rose from the dead, just as He Himself said somewhere while praying to the Father: "But You, O Lord, raise Me up, and I will repay them." Therefore, the Father who raised Him will also raise us through Him—not without the true life, that is, not without Him who says: "I am the life; he who believes in me, even if he dies, shall live; and everyone who lives and believes in me shall not die forever." Flee, then, from those godless heresies; for they are the invention of the Devil, that serpent and author of evils, who through the woman <note>Referring to Eve.</note> seduced Adam, the father of our race.

### XI.
Flee also from his evil offspring: I speak of Simon <note>Simon Magus, often cited by early Church writers as the first heretic.</note>, the firstborn of that stock, and Menander, and Basilides, and that entire collection of his wickedness; and those worshippers of a [mere] man, the Ebionites <note>Original: *Hebionitas*; a Jewish-Christian movement that believed Jesus was a mortal prophet rather than divine.</note>, whom the prophet Jeremiah asserted were accursed. Flee also those most foul Nicolaitans <note>A group mentioned in the Book of Revelation, often accused of moral compromise.</note>, falsely so named, lovers of lust and evil slanderers; for Nicolaus, the minister of the Apostles, was not such a man. Flee also the grandsons of the Most Wicked One—namely Theodotus and Cleobulus—who produce deadly fruit; if anyone tastes of it, he will die immediately, not a temporary death, but an eternal one. These all are not the planting of God the Father, but the progeny of the Accursed One. "For every plant," says God, "which my heavenly Father has not planted, shall be rooted up." If they had been branches of the Father, they certainly would not be enemies of the cross of Christ; but they belong to those who killed the Lord of glory. But now, by denying the cross and being ashamed of the passion, they cover up the iniquities of the Jews—of those, specifically, who stood as rebels against God and killed the Lord. For it is a small thing to say they were the murderers of the Prophets. Christ, therefore, invites you to His incorruption through His passion and resurrection, you who are His members.

### THE EPISTLE OF THE SAME AUTHOR<sup>1</sup> TO THE MAGNESIANS.

Ignatius, also called the God-bearer <note>original: *Theophoros*; a title meaning "one who carries God"</note>, to the church blessed<sup>2</sup> in the grace of God the Father in Christ Jesus the Savior,<sup>3</sup> in which I greet the church which is in Magnesia near the<sup>4</sup> Maeander <note>A Greek city in Ionia, modern-day Turkey</note>, and I wish it well in God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord; in whom may you have the greatest joy.

I. Recognizing your well-ordered love according to God,<sup>5</sup> I have joyfully chosen<sup>6</sup> in the faith of Jesus Christ to speak to you. For having been deemed worthy<sup>7</sup> of a divine and beloved name, in these chains which I carry about, I sing to the churches, in<sup>8</sup> which I pray for a union of the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ—who is<sup>9</sup> the Savior of all people, but especially of those who believe—by whose<sup>10</sup> blood you were redeemed; through whom you knew God, or rather were known by<sup>11</sup> Him; in whom, if you endure, you will escape all the mistreatment<sup>12</sup> of this world. # THE EPISTLE OF THE SAME AUTHOR TO THE MAGNESIANS. WRITTEN FROM SMYRNA.<sup>1</sup>

Ignatius, also called Theophorus <note>original: *Theophoros*; a title meaning "God-bearer"</note>, to the church blessed<sup>2</sup> by the grace of God the Father in Christ Jesus our Savior; in which I greet the church which is in Magnesia near the Maeander <note>An ancient Greek city in Ionia, modern-day Turkey, situated near the Maeander River</note>, and I pray in God<sup>4</sup> the Father and Christ Jesus<sup>5</sup> our Lord: in whom I wish you the greatest joy.

Having been deemed worthy of a holy and most desired name, in these chains which I carry, I sing<sup>6</sup> <note>Ignatius often uses musical metaphors to describe the harmony and praise within the Christian community</note> to the churches, in which I hope to praise [God] in the flesh and spirit of Jesus Christ,<sup>7</sup> who<sup>8</sup> is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe: by whose blood you were redeemed, through whom you have known God, or rather were known<sup>9</sup> by Him; enduring in Him, you may escape the temptation of this world. For<sup>3</sup> indeed, wisdom is not a matter of long years, nor are the elderly the only ones who<sup>4</sup> know prudence: but there is a spirit in humanity. Finally, Daniel,<sup>5</sup> being most wise at twelve<sup>6</sup> years of age, was filled with the Holy Spirit and exposed those elders, who held empty gray hair, as slanderers and seekers of someone else's beauty. Samuel<sup>7</sup> also, when he was a small boy, rebuked the ninety-year-old priest Eli<sup>8</sup> with an admonition because he honored his sons more than God. Similarly, Jeremiah<sup>9</sup> heard<sup>10</sup> from the Lord: "Do not say, 'I am a youth.'"

<meta>This page continues from page 243, continuing Ignatius's argument that the youth of a leader should not be a cause for dismissal, provided they are appointed by God. It draws heavily on Old Testament examples of young, righteous leaders and the dire consequences for those who rebel against divinely appointed authority.</meta>

<page-num>244</page-num>

->HEADER: THE LETTER OF IGNATIUS TO THE MAGNESIANS. III. IV.<-

Josiah—one who reigned at twelve years old<sup>11</sup> and delivered that fearsome and hard-to-explain judgment over the women for the sake of the children; and another who began to rule at eight years old, who cast down the altars and the sacred precincts, and burned the groves <note>The author appears to be conflating the wisdom of Solomon (who judged the two mothers) with the reforms of King Josiah. Biblical tradition usually places Josiah's accession at age eight</note>; for they were dedicated to demons, not to God. He also slaughtered the false priests as destroyers and deceivers of men, rather than worshippers of divinity. Therefore, youth is not to be despised when it is dedicated to God; rather, it is the one who is wicked in mind [who is to be despised], even if he is aged in evil days. Timothy the "Christ-bearer" <note>original: *Christophoros*; a title Ignatius often applies to holy men</note> was young; but listen to what his teacher writes to him: *Let no one despise your youth, but be an example to the believers in word and in conduct.* It is fitting, then, for you also to obey your bishop, and in no way to speak against him; for it is a fearful thing to speak against such a one. For one does not deceive this man who is seen, but plays false with the one who is invisible, who cannot be played false by anyone. Such an action has its reference not to man, but to God. For to Samuel God says: *They have not played false with you, but with me.* And Moses says: *For your grumbling is not against us, but against the Lord God.* No one remained unpunished who rose up against their superiors. For Dathan and Abiram did not speak against the law, but against Moses, and they were brought down alive into Hades. Korah and the two hundred and fifty who conspired with him against Aaron were consumed by fire. Absalom, having become a murderer of his father <note>Absalom led a rebellion against his father, King David</note>, was hung in a tree and his ill-counseling heart was pierced with arrows. Abeddadan <note>Likely a corruption of "Sheba son of Bichri" from 2 Samuel 20, or a reference to another rebel in the tradition</note> likewise had his head removed for a similar cause. Uzziah is struck with leprosy, having dared to oppose the priests and the priesthood. Saul is dishonored, not having waited for the high priest Samuel. It is necessary, then, for you also to revere your superiors.

### IV.

IV. And it is fitting not only to be called Christians, but also to be [Christians]; for it is not the name, but being so that makes one blessed. If some call someone bishop, but do everything without him, to such people he himself—who is the true and first bishop and only high priest by nature—will say: *Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do what I say?*

->### THE LETTER OF IGNATIUS TO THE MAGNESIANS. III. IV.<-

<columns>2</columns>

...I. Solomon also and Josiah appeared marvelous and wise in their works during their youth. Solomon, indeed, beginning to reign in the twelfth year of his age <note>original: *duodecimo aetatis suae anno*</note>,<sup>11</sup> resolved a difficult and inexplicable<sup>12</sup> dispute between women regarding their infants through a formidable judgment. Josiah<sup>13</sup> truly, being only eight years old, began to overturn altars and monuments, to cut down groves and throw down temples, which had been consecrated not to God, but to demons. For he also slaughtered the false priests as corruptors and deceivers of men, who served not divinity but the devil. On account of this, youth is not to be despised when it is devoted to God, but rather that age which harms one's judgment, even if it has grown old in evil days <note>A reference to the story of Susanna in the Book of Daniel 13:52</note>.<sup>14</sup> Timothy, the "Christ-bearer,"<sup>15</sup> was also a young man; but listen to what his teacher wrote to him: *Let no one*, he says, *despise your youth: but be an example to the faithful in word and in conduct.* It is right, therefore, for you to obey your Bishop, and in no way to contradict him. For it is a fearful thing to contradict such a person. For one does not merely despise this visible man, but in him mocks the one who is invisible, who cannot be mocked by anyone. This man holds his promotion not from man, but from God. For God says to Samuel<sup>17</sup> regarding those who despised him: *They have not rejected you, but me.* For Moses also said to the people who were grumbling against him:<sup>18</sup> *For your grumbling is not against us, but against the Lord God.* For no one who raised himself up against his superiors remained unpunished. Finally, in the Law, Dathan<sup>20</sup> and Abiram,<sup>21</sup> resisting Moses, were cast down alive into the underworld. But also Korah and those who conspired with him against Aaron—two hundred and fifty in number<sup>22</sup>—were consumed by fire. Absalom also,<sup>23</sup> being a parricide <note>One who kills their father; referring here to his rebellion against King David</note>, was hung from a tree by divine judgment; and his heart, which had devised evil things, was pierced with arrows. Indeed, Ahab<sup>24</sup> and Dadan were likewise beheaded for a similar cause.<sup>25</sup> Uzziah<sup>26</sup> also became a leper when he dared to seize the priesthood against the priests.<sup>27</sup> Saul<sup>28</sup> too, presuming to offer sacrifice, was stripped of his royal dignity, for he did not wait for Samuel, the prince of priests. Therefore, it is necessary for us also to revere our superiors.

# THE LETTER OF IGNATIUS TO THE MAGNESIANS. IV. V. VI. VII.

For such people do not have a good conscience, but they seem to me to be hypocrites and mere actors <note>The Greek *morphones* refers to those who put on a "form" or mask, like stage actors.</note>.

V. Since, then, all things have their end, and there lie before us two choices: life from obedience and death from disobedience; and since each person, according to their choice, is about to go to their own proper place, let us flee from death and choose life. For I say that two "characters" <note>The Greek *charaktēras* refers to the "stamp" or "impression" on a coin.</note> are found among men: one is a valid coin, the other a counterfeit forgery. The godly person is a coin stamped by God; the ungodly person is a false-named coin—deceptive, illegitimate, a forgery—not produced by God, but by the devil. I do not say that there are two "natures" of men <note>Ignatius is likely arguing against early Gnostic ideas that people are born "saved" or "damned" by nature.</note>, but rather that the one man becomes at one time a man of God, and at another a man of the devil. If a person is pious, he is a man of God; if he is impious, he is a man of the devil, becoming so not from his nature, but by his own choice. The unbelieving bear the image of the ruler of wickedness; the believing bear the image of the ruler, God the Father, and Jesus Christ. Unless we are ready to die of our own free will for the truth into His passion, His life is not in us.

VI. Since, therefore, I have seen your whole congregation in faith and love in the persons I have described, I exhort you: strive to do all things in the harmony of God. The bishop presides in the place of God, the presbyters in the place of the council of the apostles, and the deacons, who are most dear to me, are entrusted with the ministry of Jesus Christ. He was begotten by the Father before the ages, was the Word, God, the only-begotten Son; and He remains the same at the completion of the ages—for "of His kingdom there shall be no end," as Daniel the prophet says. Therefore, let us all love one another in harmony, and let no one look at his neighbor according to the flesh, but in Christ Jesus. Let there be nothing among you that is able to divide you, but be united with the bishop, submitting to God through him in Christ.

VII. Therefore, just as the Lord does nothing without the Father—for He says, "I can do nothing of myself"—so also you must do nothing without the bishop, whether you are a presbyter, a deacon, or a layman. Let nothing seem reasonable to you if it is done apart from his judgment, for such a thing is against the law and an enemy to God. Come together all at once in prayer; let there be one common petition, one mind, one hope in love,

# THE EPISTLE OF IGNATIUS TO THE MAGNESIANS. IV. V. VI. VII.

...for such people do not seem to me to have a good conscience, but to be mockers and hypocrites.

V. Since, indeed, our affairs have an end, and there lies before us life from observance <note>original: "observatione," referring here to the keeping of God's commandments</note> and death from disobedience, and it is necessary that each person be assigned in the future to the place which they have chosen for themselves from those mentioned above, let us therefore flee from death and choose life. For I say that two stamps <term>characteres: the impression or "character" stamped onto a coin to prove its value</term> are found among humans: one is the true seal of the currency, the other is counterfeit. For the godly and religious person is a true coin, which has been formed or struck by God. But the impious and irreligious person is a false coin—harmful, counterfeit, and corrupt—which was made not by God, but by the Devil. In asserting these things, I do not say that there are two natures of humans <note>Ignatius clarifies that he is not a Gnostic; he believes people are not born "good" or "evil" by nature, but become so through their choices</note>, but that it is one and the same person who at one time becomes a person of God, and at another time a person of the Devil. If anyone is godly, he is a person of God; but if anyone proves to be impious, he is of the Devil—made so not by nature, but by his own choice. For the unbelievers bear the image of the Prince of Wickedness, but the believers bear the form of the Author of all things, God the Father, and of Jesus Christ His Son. Because of this, if we do not choose to die for the truth in His passion, His life is not in us.

VI. And since I have looked upon the multitude of you in faith and love in the persons named above, I urge you to strive to do all things in the harmony of God, with the Bishop presiding in the place of God, and the Presbyters in the place of the assembly of the Apostles, and the Deacons—who are most dear to me—to whom has been entrusted the ministry of Jesus Christ, who was begotten by the Father before the ages as God the Word, the only-begotten Son: and He remains until the completion of the ages. For of His kingdom, says the Prophet Daniel, there shall be no end. Let us all love one another in harmony, and let no one regard his neighbor according to the flesh, but according to Christ Jesus. Let there be nothing among you that could separate you, but be united to the Bishop, being subject through him to God in Christ.

VII. Therefore, let nothing seem reasonable to you outside of his judgment; for such a thing is lawless and an enemy to God. All of you, come together as one for prayer. Let there be one common supplication, one mind, one hope, in blameless love in...

<meta>This page continues Ignatius’s instruction to the Magnesian church. Following his discussion on the "two stamps" of human character, he transitions into a warning against returning to Jewish legalism and "heterodox" (different) teachings, emphasizing that even the ancient prophets lived in anticipation of Christ. # THE EPISTLE OF IGNATIUS TO THE MAGNESIANS. VII. VIII. IX.

...in blameless faith, which is in Christ Jesus, than whom nothing is better. All of you, run together as into one temple of God, as to one altar, to one Jesus Christ, the High Priest of the unbegotten God.

VIII. Do not be led astray by heterodoxies <term>heterodoxiai: "different opinions" or teachings that deviate from the established faith</term>, nor pay attention to myths and endless genealogies <note>A likely reference to 1 Timothy 1:4, warning against complex speculative theories about divine emanations</note>, and Jewish vanities. Old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new. For if we still live according to Jewish law and circumcision of the flesh, we deny that we have received grace. For the most divine prophets lived according to Jesus Christ. Because of this, they were also persecuted, being inspired by His grace, to fully convince those who are disobedient <note>original: "apeithountas"</note> that there is one God the Almighty, who revealed Himself through Jesus Christ His Son, who is His Word—not a spoken word <note>original: "rhetos"</note>, but a substantial <term>ousiodes: having actual essence or being, rather than just being a fleeting sound</term> word. For He is not the utterance of articulated speech, but a generated substance of divine power, who in all things was well-pleasing to Him who sent Him.

IX. If, then, those who were brought up in the old scriptures <note>original: "en palaiois grammasin," referring to the Old Testament</note> came to a newness of hope, expecting Christ—as the Lord teaches, saying: "If you believed Moses, you would have believed me; for he wrote about me"; and, "Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day, and he saw it and was glad; for before Abraham was, I am"—how shall we be able to live without Him? Even the prophets, being His servants, foresaw Him by the Spirit and waited for Him as their teacher, and expected Him as Lord and Savior, saying: "He Himself will come and save us." Therefore, let us no longer keep the Sabbath <note>original: "sabbatizomen," meaning to observe the Jewish Saturday rest</note> in the Jewish manner, rejoicing in idleness <term>argiais: a critique of total cessation of work without spiritual purpose</term>. For "he who does not work, let him not eat." And the scriptures say, "In the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread." But let each of you keep the Sabbath spiritually, rejoicing in meditation on the law—not in relaxation of the body, but admiring the craftsmanship of God—not eating stale food <note>original: "eola," referring to food prepared the day before to avoid "work" on the Sabbath</note>, or drinking lukewarm drinks, or walking measured distances <note>A reference to the "Sabbath day's journey," a limit on how far one could walk</note>, or finding joy in dances and applause that have no meaning. And after keeping the Sabbath, let every friend of Christ celebrate the Lord’s Day <term>Kyriaken: Sunday, the "Day of the Lord"</term> as a festival—the day of the Resurrection, the queen and chief of all days. Looking forward to this day, the prophet said, "For the end, regarding the eighth" <note>Ignatius interprets Psalm headings mentioning the "eighth" as a prophecy of the "eighth day" or Sunday</note>, on which also our life dawned and the victory over death occurred in Christ. The children of perdition deny Him—the enemies of the Savior, whose...

# THE EPISTLE OF IGNATIUS TO THE MAGNESIANS. VII. VIII. IX.

...in the faith of Jesus Christ, than which nothing else is better. All of you, gather together as to the temple of God, as to one altar, to the one Jesus Christ, the High Priest of the unbegotten God the Father.

VIII. Do not be led astray by strange glories; nor pay attention to myths and endless genealogies and Jewish boastings <note>original: "inflationibus," literally "puffings up," referring to conceit or empty pride in ritual</note>; for old things have passed away, and behold, all things have become new. For if we still live according to the Jewish law and the circumcision of the flesh, we deny that we have received grace. For the holy Prophets lived according to Jesus Christ; and for this reason they also suffered persecution, being inspired by grace to manifest to the unbelieving that there is one God Almighty, who revealed Himself through Jesus Christ His Son, who is His Word—not a spoken word <note>original: "prolativum," meaning a word that is merely uttered or sounded</note> indeed, but a substantial one <term>substantiale: having a real, divine essence or "substance" rather than being a temporary sound</term>, not the speech of an articulated voice, but the operation of the Deity; a substance, that is, generated, in all things well-pleasing to the One who established Him <note>original: "substitutori," referring to the Father who sends the Son</note>.

IX. If, therefore, those who were turned from the ancient Scriptures came to a newness of hope, waiting for Christ—just as the Lord Himself teaches, saying: "If you believed Moses, you would surely believe me; for he wrote of me." And "Abraham," He says, "your father, rejoiced to see my day; and he saw it, and was glad: for before Abraham," He says, "I am"—how shall we be able to live without Him? To whom even the Prophets were servants, foreseeing Him by the Spirit; and they waited for Him as a teacher, and hoped for Him as Lord and Savior, saying: "He will come and save us." Therefore, let us not keep the Sabbath in the Jewish manner, as if rejoicing in idleness. For "he who does not work," it says, "shall not eat." And again: "In the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread," say the Oracles <note>original: "Eloquia," a term for the Holy Scriptures as the utterances of God</note>. But let each of you keep the Sabbath spiritually, rejoicing in the meditation of the Law, not in the relaxation of the body, admiring the creation of God—not like a Jew, eating things [prepared the day before] and drinking lukewarm things, and walking measured distances <note>Refers to the "Sabbath day's journey," a limited distance allowed by Rabbinic law</note>, and finding delight in dances and the clapping of hands. But instead of Sabbath-keeping, let every Christian celebrate the Lord’s Day as a festival—the day of the resurrection, the royal and most eminent of all days, concerning which the Prophet, in expectation, said: "Unto the end, for the eighth day" <note>A traditional early Christian interpretation of the titles of Psalms 6 and 11, seeing the "eighth day" as Sunday, the day beyond the seven-day week</note>: on which day also our life sprang up, and victory over death was achieved in Christ, whom the children of perdition deny—the enemies of the Savior, whose god is their belly;

<meta>This page continues the transition from Chapter IX to Chapter X of Ignatius's letter. ->### THE EPISTLE OF IGNATIUS TO THE MAGNESIANS. IX. X. XI.<-

...their god is the belly, and they mind earthly things; they are lovers of pleasure and not lovers of God, having a form of godliness but denying its power; they are "Christ-merchants" <note>original: *christemporoi* — a derogatory term for those who used the name of Christ for financial gain</note>, hawking the Word and selling Jesus; they are corrupters of women and coveters of the property of others, swept away by a storm of greed <note>original: *chrematolailapes*</note>; from whom may you be delivered by the mercy of God through our Lord Jesus Christ.

X. Let us not, therefore, be insensible to His kindness. For if He were to imitate us according to what we do, we would no longer exist. For "if You, Lord, should mark iniquities, Lord, Lord, who shall stand?" Let us therefore become worthy of the name we have received. For whoever is called by any other name more than this, he is not of God; for he has not accepted the prophecy that says concerning us: "He shall be called by a new name, which the Lord shall name him, and he shall be a holy people." This was first fulfilled in Syria; for in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians, when Paul and Peter were laying the foundation of the Church. Lay aside, therefore, the evil leaven, which has grown old and sour; and be changed into the new leaven of grace. Dwell in Christ, so that the stranger <note>original: *allotrios*, referring to the devil or an alien spirit</note> does not master you. It is absurd to speak the name of Jesus Christ with the tongue, and yet to hold onto a Judaism that has ceased in the mind; for Christianity is not Judaism <note>original: *ou gar Christianismos, ouk estin Ioudaismos*</note>; for there is one Christ, in whom every nation that has believed, and every tongue that has confessed, has been gathered together to God; and those with hearts of stone became children of God and friends of Abraham; and in his seed were blessed all those who were appointed to eternal life in Christ.

XI. These things I write, my beloved, not because I have known any of you to be in such a state, but as the least among you, I wish to warn you beforehand, lest you fall into the hooks of vain-glory, but that you may be fully convinced <term>plerophoreisthai: to be filled with certainty or fully assured</term> in Christ, who was begotten of the Father before all ages, and later born of Mary the Virgin without the company of man; who lived a holy life, and healed every disease and infirmity among the people, and performed signs and wonders for the benefit of men; and to those who had drifted into polytheism, [revealed] the one and only...

# THE EPISTLE OF IGNATIUS TO THE MAGNESIANS. XI. XII. XIII. XIV.

->...proclaiming the true God^6, His own Father; and having endured the passion, and having undergone the cross at the hands of the Christ-killing Jews under Pontius Pilate the governor and Herod the king, and having died; and having risen again, and having ascended into the heavens to Him who sent Him, and having sat down at His right hand, and coming at the consummation of the ages with paternal glory, to judge the living and the dead, and to render to each according to his works. He who knows these things with full assurance and has believed them is blessed; just as you now also are lovers of God and lovers of Christ in the full assurance of our hope, which may it happen to none of you^8 to be turned away from.<-

XII. May I have joy of you in all things, if indeed I be worthy^1; for though I am bound, I am not to be compared to even one of you who are free. I know that you are not puffed up; for you have Jesus within yourselves. And even more when I praise you, I know that you are ashamed, as it is written: *The righteous man is his own accuser* <note>Proverbs 18:17</note>; and, *Speak your sins first, that you may be justified* <note>Isaiah 43:26</note>; and, *When you have done all things that are commanded you, say that we are unprofitable servants*; for that which is high among men is an abomination before God; for God, He says, *be merciful to me a sinner*. For this reason those great men Abraham and Jacob called themselves dust and ashes before God^2; and David says, *Who am I before You, O Lord, that You have glorified me thus far?* And Moses, who was the meekest of all men, says to God: *I am thin-voiced and slow-tongued*. Be you therefore also humble^3, that you may be exalted; *for he that humbles himself^4 shall be exalted, and he that exalts himself shall be humbled*.

XIII. Strive, therefore, to be confirmed in the <term>dogmas: the established teachings or core doctrines</term> of the Lord and of the apostles, so that in all things, whatever you do, you may prosper^1 both in flesh and spirit, in faith and love, together with your most worthy bishop, and the well-woven and spiritual crown of your <term>presbytery: the council of elders or priests</term>^3, and the^4 deacons who are according to God. Be subject to the bishop and to one another, as Christ is to the Father, that there may be a union according to God among you.

XIV. Knowing that you are filled with every good thing, I have briefly exhorted you in the love of Jesus Christ. Remember me in your prayers, that I may attain to God, and the church in Syria, of which I am not worthy to be called bishop. For I need your united^1 prayer and love in God, so that the church in Syria may be deemed worthy, through your good order, to be shepherded in Christ.

# BY THE SAME AUTHOR, AN EPISTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS CONCERNING BAPTISM.<gloss>1</gloss>

Ignatius, who is also called Theophoros <note>A Greek title meaning "God-bearer"</note>, to the church of God which has found mercy in faith, patience, and love without hypocrisy, located in Philippi: mercy and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe.

I. Remembering your love and your zeal in Christ, which you have demonstrated toward us, we thought it fitting to write to your brother-loving <note>The Greek term *philadelphon* refers to the specific Christian virtue of "brotherly love"</note> soul, which is in accordance with God, to remind you of your "race" in Christ. I do this so that you may all say the same thing, being of one soul and one mind, walking by the same rule of faith, just as Paul exhorted you. For if there is one God of all things, the Father of Christ, from whom are all things; and one Lord Jesus, the Lord of all things, through whom are all things; and also one Holy Spirit, who worked in Moses, the prophets, and the apostles; and one baptism, which is administered into the death of the Lord;<gloss>2</gloss> and one<gloss>3</gloss> chosen<gloss>4</gloss> Church; then there ought<gloss>4</gloss> to be also one faith according to Christ. For there is "one Lord, one faith, one baptism; one God and Father of all, who is through all, and in all."

II. There is, therefore, one God and Father, and not two, nor three; He is the One who is, and there is no other<gloss>1</gloss> besides Him, the only true One. For it says, "The Lord your God is one Lord."<gloss>2</gloss> And again: "Did not one God create<gloss>3</gloss> us? Is there not one Father of us all?" And there is also one Son, the Word, who is God. For it says, "The only-begotten<gloss>4</gloss> Son, who is in the bosom of the Father." And again: "One Lord Jesus Christ." And in another place: "What is His name, or what is His Son’s name, that we may know it?" And there is also one Paraclete <note>A term for the Holy Spirit meaning "Advocate," "Helper," or "Comforter"</note>. For it says,<gloss>5</gloss> "There is one Spirit," since we were called in one<gloss>6</gloss> hope of our calling. And again: "We were all made to drink of one Spirit," and so forth. Clearly, one and the same Spirit works all these gifts. There are, therefore, neither three fathers, nor three sons, nor three paracletes; but one Father, and<gloss>8</gloss> one Son, and one Paraclete. Therefore, the Lord, when He sent the apostles to make disciples of all nations,<gloss>9</gloss> commanded them...

<header>THE EPISTLE OF IGNATIUS TO THE PHILIPPIANS. I. II.</header>

## EPISTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS, CONCERNING BAPTISM.
### BROUGHT BY EUPHANIUS THE READER AS HE WAS ABOUT TO BOARD THE SHIP.

Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus <note>A Greek title meaning "God-bearer"</note>, by the command of God the Father, has obtained mercy in faith, patience, and love without guile. To the Church which is at Philippi: mercy and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the Savior of all people, especially of believers.^2

I. Mindful of your charity and the concern you have in Christ, which you demonstrated toward us, we thought it fitting to write to your brotherly unity and love in the Lord, reminding you of your "race" <note>The "race" or "course" is a common Pauline metaphor for the Christian life</note> in Christ, so that you may all say the same thing, being of one mind, fixed in this very rule of faith, just as Paul says when instructing you:^6 "For there is one God of all, the Father of Christ, from whom are all things; and one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, ruler of all things, through whom are all things." And there is also one Holy Spirit, who worked in Moses and the Prophets and the Apostles. There is also one baptism, which is given into the death of Christ. Therefore, there ought to be one Church and one faith, which is in Christ, according to the saying of the same Apostle: "One Lord,^9 one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is over all, and through all, and in all."^10

II. There is therefore^1 one God and Father, and not two or three; specifically, He who is, and there is no other^2 besides Him, the only true God. "For the Lord,"^3 he says, "your God is one Lord."^4 And again: "Has not one God created us; and is there not one Father of us all?"^5 There is also one Son, God the Word. "The only-begotten," he says,^6 "who is in the bosom of the Father." And again:^7 "One Lord Jesus Christ." And elsewhere:^8 "What is His name, or what is His Son’s name?" Know also that there is one Holy Spirit,^9 the Paraclete <note>A Greek term for "Advocate" or "Comforter"</note>; as the same Paul says:^10 "One Spirit, just as you were called in one hope^11 of your calling." And again:^12 "We have all," he says, "been made to drink^13 of one spirit."^14 Clearly, the one and the same Spirit works all^15 these gifts of grace.^16 Therefore, there are neither three Fathers, nor three Sons, nor three Paracletes; but one Father, one Son, and one Paraclete. For this reason, when the Lord sent the Apostles to teach all nations, He commanded them^17 to baptize them in the name—

<page-num>266</page-num>
<header>THE EPISTLE OF IGNATIUS TO THE PHILIPPIANS. II. III. IV.</header>

...to them <note>The Apostles</note> to baptize in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; not into one person with three names <note>A reference to the Sabellian heresy, which claimed God was one person acting in three roles</note>, nor into three who became incarnate, but into three who are equal in honor.

III. For it is one who became incarnate—neither the Father nor the <term>Paraclete</term> <note>The "Comforter" or "Advocate," a title for the Holy Spirit</note>, but the Son alone. This happened not in appearance or imagination, but in truth. For "the Word <note>original: "Logos"</note> became flesh." For wisdom built a house for herself. And God the Word was born as a man, with a body from the virgin, without the involvement of a man. For "the virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son." Truly, then, he was born; truly he grew; truly he ate and drank; truly he was crucified, and died, and rose again. He who believes these things as they are, and as they happened, is blessed; he who does not believe them is accursed, no less than those who crucified the Lord. For the ruler of this world <note>Satan</note> rejoices when someone denies the cross. For he knows that the confession of the cross is his own destruction. For this is the trophy raised against his power; seeing it, he shudders, and hearing of it, he is afraid.

IV. Indeed, before the cross occurred, he <note>the devil</note> hurried for this to happen; he worked within the "sons of disobedience," working in Judas, in the Pharisees, in the Sadducees, in the elders, in the young, and in the priests. But as it was about to happen, he became troubled and cast a sense of regret into the traitor <note>Judas</note>, showing him a noose and teaching him how to hang himself. He also terrified the woman <note>Pilate's wife</note>, disturbing her with dreams, and he tried to stop the events of the cross—he who "moves every rope" <note>An ancient Greek proverb meaning to leave no stone unturned or to try every possible means</note> toward his own preparation. He did not repent for such great evil—for if he had, he would not be entirely wicked—but he perceived his own destruction. For the cross of Christ is the beginning of his condemnation, the beginning of his death, and the beginning of his ruin. Therefore, he also works in some people to deny the cross, to be ashamed of the passion, to call the death a mere "appearance" <note>The "Docetic" heresy, which claimed Jesus only seemed to have a physical body and suffer</note>, to cut out the birth from the virgin, and to slander nature itself as something defiled. He fights alongside the Jews in their denial of the cross, with the Greeks in their slanderous claims of magic, and with the heretics in their talk of "imaginary" bodies. For the general of wickedness is multifaceted, a thief of minds, unstable, and inconsistent with himself; putting forward one thing while showing another. For he is wise in doing evil, but he is ignorant of what is good; for he is filled with ignorance due to a voluntary madness. For how is he not such a one, who cannot even see the logic <note>original: "logos"</note> right before his feet?

...of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; not into someone who is one with three names <note>original: "trinomium." This refers to the Sabellian heresy, which taught that God is one person who simply wears three different "masks" or names</note>, nor into three who share the same honor <note>This likely argues against the idea of three separate Gods (tritheism) or that all three persons of the Trinity became human</note>.

III. Because there is only one who was made man; it was certainly not the Father, nor the <term>Paraclete</term> <note>The "Advocate" or "Helper," a title for the Holy Spirit</note>, but the Son alone. This happened not supposedly¹ or as a phantom <note>original: "phantasmate." This refutes "Docetism," the belief that Jesus only *seemed* to have a physical body</note>, but in most certain truth. "For the Word <note>original: "Verbum," translating the Greek "Logos"</note> became flesh, and dwelt² within it." "For Wisdom built a house for herself." And God the Word became like a human being, with the body which he took from a virgin: not, of course, from sexual intercourse or the seed of a man. "For a virgin," he says,³ "shall conceive in her womb, and shall bear a son." Truly, therefore,⁴ he was born, and truly he grew; truly he ate,⁵ and drank; truly he was crucified and died, and rose again. He who believes these things as they are, in the manner he was born, is blessed. But he who does not believe these things is no less than those who crucified him.⁶ For the prince of this world <note>Satan</note> rejoices in this: when anyone denies the cross. For he knows that the confession of the cross is his own destruction. For this is the trophy raised against his power: seeing it, he is terrified, and hearing of it, he is afraid.

IV. For even before the cross had happened,¹ he was hurrying to bring this about, and he worked within the children² of distrust. He worked moreover in Judas,³ in the Pharisees, in the Sadducees, in the elders, in the youths, and in⁴ the Priests. But when he was rushing for it to happen, he became troubled;⁵ and afterwards he sent despair⁶ upon the traitor, showing him the noose and teaching him how to hang himself. He also sent fear into the woman <note>Pilate's wife</note> in a dream—he himself causing the disturbance and trying to check the execution on the cross, he himself calling out and moving all things for his own preparation, not recognizing [the outcome]: for not all things were so⁷ evil. But the Evil One felt his own ruin.⁸ For the cross of Christ was the beginning of his condemnation, the starting point of death, the beginning of perdition. Because of this, he works in some to deny the cross and to be ashamed of the passion: those who think to call the birth from the Virgin a "death," who circumcise nature itself, and defame it as if it were hateful. He is the helper of the Jews⁹ toward the denial of the cross, of the Pagans toward the slander of magic, and of the Heretics toward the idea of a phantom appearance. For the prince of malice is¹⁰ multiform, stealing away the senses, contradicting himself; putting forward some things, while displaying others. For he is wise¹¹ at doing evil; but as for what is good, he never knows it. For he is filled with ignorance¹² through disobedience. For how could he not be such a one, who does not set his own word before himself?

V. For if the Lord was a mere man, consisting of soul and body
alone, why do you strip away the birth that is common to human nature?
And why, as if something paradoxical were happening to a man, do you call
his suffering an "appearance"? <note>original: "dokesin." This refers to Docetism, the belief that Jesus only *seemed* to suffer</note> And why do you consider the death of a mortal to be a mere
reputation? But if he is both God and man, why do you call the Lord of glory
"lawless," <note>The author is likely addressing the devil or a heretic who claims Christ's actions broke the Law</note> him who is by nature unchangeable? Why do you call the lawgiver "lawless,"
the one who possesses a human<gloss>1</gloss> soul? The Word became flesh, and was a
perfect man, not merely dwelling within a man. And how is he a "magician," 
this one who of old fashioned every nature—perceivable and intellectual—
by the will of the Father; and in his incarnation<gloss>2</gloss> healed every disease 
and infirmity?

VI. And how is this one not God,<gloss>1</gloss> who raises the dead, sending away the lame
made whole, cleansing lepers, giving sight to the blind, either increasing 
or transforming existing things—such as the five loaves and<gloss>2</gloss> the two fish,
and the water into wine—and putting your army to flight with a word alone?
And why do you disparage the nature of the virgin, and call her body parts 
shameful?<gloss>3</gloss> You who of old paraded these things, and commanded people 
to be stripped naked—men before the eyes of women, and women<gloss>4</gloss> to the 
unrestrained desire of men. Now these things have been deemed shameful by 
you, and you pretend to be dignified,<gloss>5</gloss> you who are the spirit of fornication; 
ignorant that something only becomes shameful when lawlessness is 
woven into it. But where sin is absent, none of the things created are 
shameful, nothing is base, but all are "very good." And you, not seeing 
this, disparage them?

VII. And how, again, does it no longer seem to you that Christ is from the
virgin, but is the God over all, the Almighty? Tell me then, who is it who 
sent him? Who is the one who has authority over him? By whose will did 
he obey?<gloss>1</gloss> Of what laws<gloss>2</gloss> did he become the fulfiller, he who yields neither 
to the will nor the authority of anyone? And by removing Christ from 
his birth, you legislate<gloss>3</gloss> that the Unbegotten was born, and that the One 
without beginning was nailed to a cross. By whose permission, I cannot 
say; but indeed you have not escaped my notice,<gloss>4</gloss> you double-dealer! Nor 
am I ignorant that you walk by crooked and double paths.<gloss>5</gloss> But you, who 
pretend to know everything, are ignorant of who it was that was born.

VIII. For many things escape you: the virginity<gloss>1</gloss> of Mary; the 
paradoxical birth; who it was in the body; the star that led those in the 
East, the Magi who brought gifts; the Archangel’s greeting to the virgin; 
the paradoxical conception of the betrothed virgin; the proclamation<gloss>2</gloss> 
of the child-forerunner regarding the one from the virgin, and his leaping 
in the womb because of the one being beheld beforehand; the hymns of 
the angels over the one who was born; the shepherds’ good tidings—

V. For if the Lord were a mere man, consisting only of soul and body, why do you curtail the birth that is common to the nature of men? Why do you call his suffering a "simulation" <note>This refers to the heresy of Docetism, from the Greek *dokein* (to seem), which claimed Christ only appeared to be human</note>—as if it were a minor glory manifested in a man—and why do you consider the death of a mortal to be a mere reputation? If he is both God and<sup>1</sup> man, why do you call the Lord of glory "lawless,"<sup>2</sup> him who is clearly unchangeable by nature?<sup>3</sup> Why do you call the Lawgiver "lawless," as if he did not possess a human soul? The Word<sup>4</sup> was made flesh; the Word was man, but not [merely] dwelling *within* a man. How then is he a "magician,"<sup>5</sup> he who in the beginning prepared every sensible and intelligible<sup>6</sup> nature by the will of the Father? He who, while he was in the flesh, healed every infirmity<sup>7</sup> and weakness?

VI. And how is he not God,<sup>1</sup> he who raised the dead, healed the lame, cleansed the lepers, gave sight to the blind, and satisfied so many thousands of men from five loaves and two fish,<sup>2</sup> turned water into wine, and put your army to flight by a word alone? <note>Addressing the devil, whose "army" of demons Christ cast out</note> Why then do you disparage the nature of the Virgin and call her members shameful? You, who once sowed these [shameful acts] and ordered males to be naked in the presence of females, and females to be driven into unlawful desire for males. Now all things seem shameful to you, and you pretend to be modest, though you are the spirit of fornication. Do you not know that something becomes<sup>3</sup> shameful only when it is performed unlawfully? Otherwise, nothing is shameful that is conducted without sin; nothing is depraved, but all things are "very good." And do you, being blind, disparage them?

VII. How, again, does it not seem to you that Christ is from a virgin, but rather that he is the God who is over all, namely the Almighty? Tell me, then: who is it that sent him? Or who is it that rules over him? To whose judgment was he subject, or whose law did he fulfill? You, who—possessing the judgment or power of no one<sup>1</sup>—separate Christ from his birth, and pronounce the Lawgiver to be unbegotten, and claim the one without beginning was fixed to a cross. By whose permission this was done,<sup>2</sup> I cannot say. For you have not escaped my notice with your ancient plan; nor am I ignorant that you walk crookedly and slippery. But you are ignorant of who<sup>3</sup> it is that was born, you who<sup>4</sup> pretend to know all things.

For if you had known that he was the Son of God,¹¹ you would have known that he who kept his body without need for forty days and as many¹² nights, could have done this¹³ forever. Why then¹⁴ does he hunger? In order to show that he truly took on¹⁵ a body with the same feelings as men; for through the first [the fast], he showed that he was God; but through the second [the hunger], that he was also man.

X. You, then, who fell from the highest glory like lightning, do you dare to say to the Lord, "Throw yourself down from here"? Do you say this to Him for whom all existing things are accounted as nothing? And do you challenge to vainglory Him who does not seek display? You even pretend to read the Scripture concerning Him:
> "For He shall give His angels charge over thee, and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone." <note>This is a quote from Psalm 91:11–12, used by the devil during the temptation of Jesus in the wilderness.</note>

And you pretend to be ignorant of the rest, stealing away those things which were prophesied concerning you and your servants:
> "You shall tread upon the asp and the basilisk, and you shall trample the lion and the dragon underfoot." <note>Psalm 91:13. The author notes that Satan conveniently stops quoting the Psalm before it reaches the verse predicting his own defeat.</note>

XI. If, therefore, you are a footstool for the Lord's feet, how can you tempt the One who cannot be tempted, forgetting the Lawgiver who commanded:
> "Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God"? <note>Deuteronomy 6:16.</note>

But you even dare, most polluted one, to claim the works of God as your own, and to say that the rule over these things has been delivered to you. You hold out your own fall as a threat to the Lord, and you promise to give His own things back to Him if He will fall down upon the earth and worship you? And how did you not shudder to let such a voice go out against the Master, O spirit more wicked than all wicked spirits, born of a malicious mind? You were defeated by the stomach <note>A reference to the first temptation: turning stones into bread.</note>, and you were dishonored by vainglory; by the love of money and the love of power, you are dragged into impiety. You are Beliar <note>A name for the devil meaning "worthless."</note>, the dragon, the apostate, the crooked serpent, the one who revolted from God, the one who was separated from Christ, the one who was alienated from the Holy Spirit, the one who was cast out from the choir of angels, the abuser of the laws of God, the enemy of all that is lawful, the one who rose up against the first-formed humans <note>Adam and Eve.</note> and cast out from the commandment those who had done you no wrong, the one who roused the murderer Cain against Abel, the one who campaigned against Job—do you say to the Lord: "If you fall down and worship me"? Oh, what audacity! Oh, what madness! A runaway slave, a slave deserving of the lash, you rebel against your good Master. To such a Master, to the God of all things perceived by the mind and the senses, do you say: "If you fall down and worship me"?

XII. But the Lord is long-suffering, and does not destroy into non-existence the one who, out of ignorance, behaves so boldly; rather, He answers mildly:
> "Get away, Satan." <note>Matthew 4:10.</note>

He did not say, "Get behind me," <note>original: "Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου"</note> for it is not possible for you to return <note>The author argues that while Peter was told "Get behind me" to return to his place as a follower, the devil is simply told to "Go away" because he is beyond repentance.</note>; but rather:
> "Get away, Satan, into those things you have chosen; go away into those things where you were stirred up by a malicious mind. For I know who I am, and by whom I have been sent, and I understand whom it is necessary to worship. For thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and Him only shalt thou serve."

<header>IGNATIUS'S EPISTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS. XII. XIII. XIV. XV.</header>

...only <note>The text continues from the previous page where Ignatius addresses Satan.</note> Him, of whom you have become a rebel. I am not an adversary of God; I acknowledge His supremacy. I know the Cause of my existence: the Father.

XIII. These things, brothers, I have been compelled to write to you out of my affection for you, exhorting you for the glory of God—not as if I were someone of importance, but as your brother. Be subject to the bishop, the elders, and the deacons. Love one another in the Lord, as images of God. Husbands, see that you love your wives as your own members; wives, love your husbands as being one in your union. If anyone remains chaste or practices self-control, let him not be prideful, so that he does not lose his reward. Do not dishonor the feast days; do not despise the <term>forty-day fast</term><note>The term "Quadragesima" or Lent, representing the forty days of fasting practiced by Christ.</note>, for it contains an imitation of the Lord’s way of life. After the week of the Passion, do not neglect to fast on Wednesday and Friday, distributing your surplus to the poor. If anyone fasts on the Lord’s Day <note>Sunday</note> or on the Sabbath <note>Saturday</note>, except for the one Sabbath of Passover <note>Holy Saturday</note>, he is a <term>murderer of Christ</term><note>original: "christoktonos." A very harsh term used in the early church to describe those who violated fasting laws or liturgical traditions that separated Christian identity from Jewish practice.</note>.

XIV. Let your prayers be extended to the church of Antioch, from where I am being led away as a prisoner to Rome. I greet the holy bishop Polycarp; I greet the holy bishop Vitalius, and the sacred council of elders, and my fellow-servants the deacons—at the cost of whose souls may I be redeemed. <note>original: "antipsychos." A term used by Ignatius to express a deep, sacrificial bond with his colleagues.</note> Furthermore, I submit myself to the bishop and the elders in the Lord. If anyone celebrates the Passover with the Jews, or receives the symbols of their feast, he is a companion of those who killed the Lord and His apostles.

XV. Philo and Agathopus the deacons greet you. I greet the assembly of virgins and the order of widows—may I have joy in them. I greet the people of the Lord, from the least to the greatest. I have sent this letter to you through Euphanius the reader, a man honored by God and most faithful, whom I met near <term>Rhegium</term><note>A city on the "toe" of Italy, modern Reggio Calabria.</note> as he was setting sail in a ship. Remember my chains, that I may be perfected in Christ. Fare well in flesh, soul, and spirit, being of a perfect mind, turning away from workers of iniquity and the corrupters of the word of truth; be strengthened in the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.

## EPISTLE OF THE SAME AUTHOR TO THE PHILADELPHIANS.<gloss>1</gloss>

Ignatius, who is also called <term>Theophorus</term><note>Greek: *Theophoros*, meaning "God-bearer." This was a title Ignatius used to describe himself as one who carries Christ within his soul.</note>, to the church of God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, located in Philadelphia, which has received mercy in love and is firmly established in the harmony of God, and which rejoices<gloss>2</gloss> in the passion of our Lord Jesus Christ<gloss>3</gloss> without wavering, and is fully assured in His resurrection with all mercy. I greet this church in the blood of Jesus Christ, which is eternal and lasting joy; especially for those<gloss>4</gloss> who are at one<gloss>5</gloss> with the bishop and the presbyters and the deacons, who have been appointed by the will of God the Father through the Lord Jesus Christ. According to His own will,<gloss>6</gloss> He has firmly established His church upon the rock, as a spiritual building<gloss>7</gloss> not made with human hands. Even when the winds and the floods beat against it, they were not able to overturn it; nor may the spiritual forces of wickedness ever have the power to do so, but may they be weakened by the power of Jesus Christ our Lord.

I. Having observed your bishop, I recognized that he was not appointed to this ministry—which belongs to the whole community—from himself or through men, nor through <term>vainglory</term><note>Greek: *kenodoxia*, meaning empty pride or the desire for human praise.</note>, but in the love of Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead. I am struck with amazement<gloss>8</gloss> at his forbearance<gloss>9</gloss>; by his silence, he is more powerful than those who speak at great length.<gloss>10</gloss> For he is as harmoniously attuned to the commandments of the Lord and His decrees as the strings are to a harp. He is blameless, no less than <term>Zechariah the priest</term><note>A reference to the father of John the Baptist, described in the Gospel of Luke as walking blamelessly in the Lord's commandments.</note>. Therefore, my soul blesses his godly mind, recognizing it to be virtuous and perfect, as well as his unwavering and calm nature in all the forbearance of the living God.

II. As children of the light of truth, flee from the division of unity and the evil teaching<gloss>1</gloss> of the heretics, from whom a defilement has gone out into all the earth. Where the shepherd is, there you should follow as sheep;<gloss>2</gloss> for many wolves in sheep’s clothing take captive those who run the race of God by means of a wicked pleasure; but in your unity, they find no place.

III. Keep yourselves away from the evil herbs [weeds], which Jesus Christ does not cultivate, but rather the man-slaying beast, because they are not<gloss>1</gloss>

### THE EPISTLE OF THE SAME AUTHOR TO THE PHILADELPHIANS. FROM TROAS.<gloss>1</gloss>

Ignatius, who is also called <term>Theophorus</term><note>A Greek title meaning "God-bearer." It signifies one who carries the Spirit of God or Christ within them.</note>, to the Church of God the Father and of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is in Philadelphia, having obtained mercy in love, and being established in the harmony and exultation of God, wavering not in the passion of our Lord, and in His resurrection being filled with all mercy: which I also salute in the blood of Jesus Christ, which is eternal and unique joy: especially to those<gloss>2</gloss> who are at one with the Bishop and with the <term>Presbyters</term><note>The "elders" or priests of the early church community.</note> and with the <term>Deacons</term><note>Ministers appointed to assist the bishops and elders, particularly in service to the poor.</note>, who have been approved in the will of God the Father, through the Lord Jesus Christ, who according to His own will firmly established His Church upon the rock, as a spiritual building<gloss>3</gloss> not made by human hands, which the flooding rivers and blowing winds were not able to overturn; nor may the spirits of wickedness ever prevail, but let them be weakened by the power of our Lord Jesus Christ.

I. Having seen your Bishop, I recognize that he was promoted to the ministry pertaining to the community not by his own effort, nor by men,<gloss>4</gloss> nor through <term>vainglory</term><note>Meaning empty pride or the pursuit of human applause.</note>,<gloss>5</gloss> but in the love of Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead: I am struck with awe by his gentleness, and how, by remaining silent, he has more power than one who speaks.<gloss>6</gloss> For he is as attuned to the commandments of the Lord and His justice as the strings<gloss>7</gloss> are to a lyre; and he is irreproachable,<gloss>8</gloss> no less than the priest Zechariah.<gloss>9</gloss> On account of this, my soul blesses his disposition toward God,<gloss>10</gloss> knowing it to be innocent and<gloss>11</gloss> perfect and unshakable, and his gentleness toward all, which is without anger, as that of the living God.

II. Therefore, as<gloss>1</gloss> children of light, truly<gloss>2</gloss> flee from the division of unity and the evil doctrine<gloss>3</gloss> of the Heretics, from<gloss>4</gloss> whom a defilement has gone out into all the earth. Where the Shepherd is, therefore,<gloss>5</gloss> there gather together as sheep.<gloss>6</gloss> For many<gloss>7</gloss> wolves in sheep's clothing, with evil intent,<gloss>8</gloss> take captive those who are running toward God; but in your unity they find no place.

III. Therefore, keep yourselves away from evil words,<gloss>1</gloss> which Jesus Christ did not sow, but rather that beast which kills men: because these are not plant-

...the planting of the *Father*, but the seed of the evil one. I do not write these things because I found division among you, but I am warning you beforehand as children of God; for as many as belong to Christ, these are with the bishop; but as many as turn away from him and embrace fellowship with those under a curse, these shall be cut off along with them; for they are not the husbandry of Christ, but the sowing of the enemy; may you always be delivered from this by the prayers of your presiding shepherd, most faithful and most gentle. I exhort you therefore in the Lord: as many as may repent and come to the unity of the church, receive them with all gentleness, so that through goodness and patience, having recovered from the snare of the devil and having become worthy of Jesus Christ, they may obtain eternal salvation in the kingdom of Christ. Brethren, be not deceived; if anyone follows one who creates a schism from the truth, he shall not inherit the kingdom of God; and if anyone does not depart from the false-speaking preacher, he shall be condemned to <term>Gehenna</term><note>A term for the place of fiery judgment, often used in the New Testament to denote hell.</note>; for it is not right to depart from the godly, nor is it fitting to associate with the ungodly. If anyone walks in a strange opinion, he is not of Christ, nor a partaker of His passion; but he is a fox, a destroyer of Christ's vineyard. Do not mix with such a person, lest you perish with him; even if he be a father, or a son, or a brother, or a kinsman. For "your eye shall not spare him," it says. It is necessary for you also to hate those who hate God and to pine away over His enemies; yet not to strike them or persecute them, as do the nations who know not the Lord and God; but to consider them enemies and separate from them; yet to admonish them and exhort them to repentance, if perhaps they might hear, if perhaps they might yield. For our God is a lover of humanity, and "desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth"; therefore "He makes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous"; the Lord, wishing us also to be imitators of His goodness, says: "Be perfect, even as your heavenly *Father* is perfect."

### IV.
I have confidence in you in the Lord, that you will be of no other mind; therefore I write with boldness to your God-worthy love, exhorting you to use one faith, and one preaching, and one <term>Eucharist</term><note>The ritual of the Lord's Supper or Holy Communion. Ignatius emphasizes that there should only be one such celebration in a city to maintain unity.</note>; for there is one flesh of the Lord Jesus, and one blood of His which was poured out for us; one bread also was broken for all, and one cup distributed to all; one altar for the whole church, and one bishop, together with the <term>presbytery</term><note>The council of elders or priests who assisted the bishop.</note> and the deacons, my fellow-servants.

[...the planting] of the Father, but the nursery of the Most Evil One. I write these things to you not because I have found division among you, but because I have found you to be children of God. For as many as belong to Christ, these are with the **Bishop**. But those who turn away from him, or from his communion, and associate themselves with those under a curse, they shall be cut off along with them. For they are not the workers of Christ, but the nursery of the Enemy; may you always be delivered from them through the prayers of your most faithful and most gentle presiding Shepherd. I therefore plead with you in the Lord: whoever returns in repentance to the unity of the Church, receive them with all gentleness, so that through their usefulness and good display, having been delivered from the mud and the <term>snare</term><note>Latin: *muscipula*, literally a mousetrap; here used metaphorically for the traps of the devil.</note> of the Devil and made worthy of Jesus Christ, they may receive eternal salvation in the kingdom of Christ. Do not be deceived, brothers. For whoever follows one who is separated from the truth shall not inherit the kingdom of God; and whoever does not distance themselves from a false-speaking preacher shall be condemned to <term>Gehenna</term><note>A reference to a place of fiery judgment or hell.</note>. Therefore, it is necessary neither to depart from the righteous nor to draw near to the unrighteous. For whoever walks in a foreign opinion is not of Christ, nor a sharer in His passion, but is a deceiver and a corrupter of Christ's vineyard. Do not associate with such a person, lest you perish along with him: not even if he is a father, or a son, or a brother, or a member of the household. "For," it says, "let your eye not spare him." <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 13:8 or Ezekiel 9:5 regarding divine judgment.</note> Therefore, those who hate God, it is necessary for you also to hate them, and to grieve over His enemies. Indeed, it is not necessary for us to persecute or strike them, after the manner of the <term>Gentiles</term><note>Meaning the non-Christian nations or pagans who do not know the biblical God.</note> who do not know God; but to consider them enemies, and to separate from them, and to warn them, and to call them to repentance, if perhaps they might listen and comply. For our God is a lover of humanity, and He wants all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. For this reason, He makes His sun to rise over the good and the evil, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous. Wishing us to be imitators of this goodness, the Lord says: "Be perfect, just as your heavenly Father is perfect."

...for there is also one Unbegotten <note>Greek: *agennētos*; meaning without origin or uncreated, a term used to distinguish God the Father from the Son.</note>, God and Father; and one Only-begotten Son, God the Word and man; and one Comforter, the Spirit of truth; and also one preaching, and one faith, and one baptism, and one church, which the holy apostles established from one end of the earth to the other, in the blood of Christ, by their own sweat and labors. And you, therefore, as a "chosen people and a holy nation," <note>A reference to 1 Peter 2:9.</note> must accomplish all things in Christ with harmony. 

Wives, be subject to your husbands in the fear of God; virgins, be subject to Christ in incorruption, not loathing marriage, but desiring that which is better <note>A reference to the ascetic choice of celibacy over marriage, though the author is careful not to condemn marriage itself.</note>; not for the sake of slandering union, but for the sake of meditating on the law. Children, obey your parents, and cherish them as fellow-workers with God for your birth. Slaves, be subject to your masters in God, so that you may become the "freedmen of Christ." <note>A reference to 1 Corinthians 7:22.</note> Husbands, love your wives as fellow-servants of God, as your own body, as partners in life, and as helpers in the procreation of children. 

Virgins, keep only Christ before your eyes and His Father in your prayers, being enlightened by the Spirit. May I have joy in your holiness, like that of Elijah, <note>The textual variant notes Elijah here.</note> like that of Joshua the son of Nun, like Melchizedek, like Elisha, like Jeremiah, like John the Baptist, like the beloved disciple <note>The Apostle John.</note>, like Timothy, like Titus, like Evodius <note>The first Bishop of Antioch before Ignatius.</note>, like Clement, who departed this life in purity. 

Yet I do not blame the other blessed ones because they entered into marriages, those whom I have just remembered; for I pray, having been found worthy of God, to be found at their footsteps in the kingdom—such as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, such as Joseph and Isaiah and the other prophets; such as Peter and Paul and the other apostles who were joined in marriages. They did not enter these unions out of a passion for the act, but out of a concern for the continuation of the human race. 

Fathers, bring up your children in the discipline and admonition of the Lord; and teach them the sacred scriptures and crafts, so that they may not take pleasure in idleness. "A righteous father," it says, "brings up his child well; the heart of a wise son shall rejoice." <note>A paraphrased reference to Proverbs 23:24.</note> Masters, attend to your servants with kindness, as holy Job taught; for there is one nature, and one race of humanity; for in Christ there is neither slave nor free. 

Rulers, let them obey Caesar; soldiers, obey the rulers; deacons, obey the presbyters <note>Priests.</note> as high priests; the presbyters, the deacons, and the rest of the clergy, along with all the people and the soldiers and the rulers and Caesar, let them obey the **Bishop**; and the **Bishop** obeys...
